rules.name: Industrial Torch Vendor Investigation

direction.title: Investigate Industrial Torch / Cutting Equipment Vendors
direction.description: Query registered industrial cutting equipment vendors within 100km radius. Professional gangs typically source oxy-acetylene torches, plasma cutters, and angle grinders from legitimate suppliers using shell companies or stolen identities.
direction.trigger: Professional gang hypothesis is strong and specialised cutting/entry technique is indicated by the scene evidence.
direction.expected_outcome: Identifies the procurement or rental trail for the cutting equipment used at the scene, and any names/companies behind it.

rules.why_template: Professional gang hypothesis is strong and document evidence exists — suggesting organized procurement of industrial equipment through registered channels.

rules.name: Vehicle Movement Analysis

direction.title: Multi-Source Vehicle Tracking
direction.description: Correlate vehicle movements using FASTag toll data, ANPR systems, fuel pump CCTV, GPS breadcrumbs, and highway surveillance cameras. Professional gangs often use stolen or cloned vehicles.
direction.trigger: A vehicle (stolen/forged plates, unregistered, or unusual) is tied to the scene or escape and the professional-gang hypothesis is above 60%.
cross_match: Fuel stops against known safe-house areas
direction.expected_outcome: Reconstructs the vehicle's route before and after the incident, narrowing down escape direction and possible drop points.

rules.why_template: Vehicle evidence detected with professional gang hypothesis above 60% — multi-source tracking can reveal escape routes, safe houses, and accomplice networks.

rules.name: Specialised Equipment Procurement (RF Jammer / Tactical Gear)

direction.title: Trace RF Jammer / Tactical Equipment Procurement
direction.description: RF jammers, suppressors, and tactical communication gear are not everyday-market items — sourcing one is itself a procurement lead, not just a weapon. Trace vendor, purchaser, payment, and delivery for any such equipment referenced in the scene evidence.
direction.trigger: Professional-gang hypothesis is strong and scene evidence indicates specialised/tactical equipment (signal jamming, suppressed weapons, coordinated team gear) rather than opportunistic tools.
search_targets: Payment gateway records tied to such purchases
direction.expected_outcome: Identifies who acquired the specialised equipment and how, often surfacing a name, phone number, or delivery address linked to the team.

rules.why_template: Specialised/tactical equipment implies a deliberate procurement step — tracing it is often faster than tracing the crime itself.

rules.name: Escape Route Reconstruction

direction.title: Reconstruct Escape Route (Scene → Last Known Point)
direction.description: Build a geographic timeline from the last confirmed scene sighting to the vehicle's last known location: road network, CCTV/ANPR chokepoints, fuel stops, bridges/tollways, and any abandonment or hand-off site.
direction.trigger: A clear exit event exists in the timeline (e.g. vehicle departure, device/GPS loss) but the route beyond that point is still unknown.
cross_match: Timestamp of exit against camera timestamps along candidate routes
Abandonment site against known associate addresses
direction.expected_outcome: Narrows the search area for the team's safe house or onward transport, and may recover the vehicle itself as physical evidence.
failure_conditions: No cameras along the escape corridor
Extended time gap before search began

rules.why_template: The timeline shows a clear exit point but the route afterward is unresolved — this is a distinct, high-value investigation direction in its own right, not just evidence collection.
